Michalovce Jewish Cemetery in Straniany

Jewish Cemetery · Michalovce, Slovakia

Not demolished. A small Jewish community existed in Straniany, across the Laborec River, dependent on Michalovce but with its own rabbi and prayer house; this cemetery's oldest tombstones date to the 1890s, and it remained in use until 1925, when Straniany was joined to Michalovce and its Jews began using the cemetery at Hrádek, documented elsewhere in this collection. According to Michalovce's own Yizkor memorial book, an even older cemetery — in fact the first Jewish cemetery serving Michalovce itself — once stood in Straniany, existing since the end of the 18th century, though its exact location remains unknown; one researcher connects it to the 1797 founding of the Michalovce Chevra Kadisha in the Straniany prayer house. Emil Knieza, a Holocaust survivor from Michalovce, recalled hearing of a still older cemetery near the Laborec river, said by some to date to the 16th or 17th century — a claim requiring further research to confirm.
